title: C# Questions & Answers - Character Stream
sourceFile: Character Stream - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on character streams of C# Programming Language.

questions.question: From which of these base classes is the character-based output class 'StreamWriter' derived?
questions.explanation: In C#, 'StreamWriter' inherits from the abstract 'TextWriter' class, which is designed for sequential character output.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using character stream-based file handling over byte streams?

options.text: They operate directly on Unicode characters
They use less memory than byte streams

questions.explanation: Character streams (TextReader/TextWriter and StreamReader/StreamWriter) read and write text using an Encoding. Byte streams work with raw bytes. In modern .NET, StreamWriter defaults to UTF-8, not a raw 16-bit dump of System.Char.

questions.question: Which class is specifically used to perform character-based read operations from a file?
questions.explanation: 'StreamReader' is designed to read characters from a byte stream (like 'FileStream') using a specific encoding.

questions.question: Which method is used to clear all data present in output buffers and write them to the underlying stream?
questions.explanation: The 'Flush()' method ensures that any data previously written to the buffer is immediately moved to the destination device.

questions.question: Which method of 'TextReader' attempts to read a specified number of characters into a buffer and blocks until they are read?

options.text: int Read(char[] buffer, int index, int count)
int ReadBlock(char[] buffer, int index, int count)

questions.explanation: 'ReadBlock' is similar to 'Read', but it blocks until either 'count' characters have been read or the end of the stream is reached.

questions.question: In the method 'int Read(char[] buffer, int index, int count)', what does the 'index' parameter specify?

options.text: The total number of characters to read
The starting position in the 'buffer' array at which to begin writing
The position in the file to start reading from

questions.explanation: The 'index' parameter refers to the offset in the destination array ('buffer'), not the position in the source file.

questions.question: Which method obtains the next character from the input stream without consuming it, returning -1 if no characters are available?
questions.explanation: The 'Peek()' method allows you to look at the next character without moving the internal stream pointer.

questions.question: Which concept is used to perform all input and output operations in C#?
questions.explanation: In .NET, a 'Stream' is an abstraction of a sequence of bytes, used for all types of I/O (files, network, memory).

questions.question: What are the two primary types of streams defined in the C# System.IO namespace?
questions.explanation: .NET categorizes I/O into byte-oriented (Stream class) and character-oriented (TextReader/TextWriter classes).

questions.question: In the constructor 'StreamWriter(string path, bool append)', what happens if 'append' is set to true?

options.text: The file is opened for reading only
The file is deleted and recreated
New data is added to the end of the existing file

questions.explanation: If 'append' is true, data will be written at the end of the file. If false, the file is overwritten.
